principle.name: Business-First Naming
principle.description: Use business-friendly names for datasets, fields, and metrics. Avoid technical table column names as the primary identifier.
principle.rationale: OSI models serve as the semantic layer between physical data and AI/BI tools. Business names improve discoverability and query generation.

principle.name: Comprehensive ai_context
principle.description: Every entity (model, dataset, field, metric, relationship) should include ai_context with synonyms and instructions.
principle.rationale: AI tools rely on ai_context to understand business meaning and generate accurate queries. Rich synonyms improve LLM query generation.

principle.name: Multi-Dialect Expressions
principle.description: When a model targets multiple platforms, provide dialect-specific expressions for critical fields and metrics.
principle.rationale: Different platforms have different SQL syntax. Multi-dialect support ensures portability across Snowflake, Databricks, and ANSI SQL environments.

example.good: dialects: [{dialect: ANSI_SQL, expression: "a || b"}, {dialect: SNOWFLAKE, expression: "CONCAT(a, b)}]

principle.name: Time Dimension Marking
principle.description: Mark all time-related fields with dimension.is_time: true to enable temporal filtering and time-series analysis.
principle.rationale: AI tools use is_time flags to automatically apply time-based operations like date truncation and rolling windows.

principle.name: Composite Key Documentation
principle.description: Document both primary_key and unique_keys explicitly. Use composite keys when single columns cannot uniquely identify rows.
principle.rationale: Relationship resolution depends on accurate key information. Missing unique_keys can cause incorrect join paths.

convention.rule: Use lowercase with underscores for all OSI entity names
Use database.schema.table format for dataset source references
Use unqualified column names in field expressions; qualify in metric expressions
Place version header and schema reference at file top

pitfall.description: Forgetting to mark time dimensions with is_time: true
pitfall.why_problematic: AI tools cannot automatically apply time-based operations without this flag
pitfall.correct_approach: Review all date/datetime columns and set dimension.is_time: true

pitfall.description: Using raw SQL column names instead of business names
pitfall.why_problematic: Reduces AI query generation quality and discoverability
pitfall.correct_approach: Use business-friendly names; add technical column as expression if different

pitfall.why_problematic: LLMs may not recognize alternative terms users might use in natural language queries
pitfall.correct_approach: Add common synonyms, abbreviations, and business terms to ai_context

pitfall.why_problematic: Relationships with incorrect column references break join path resolution
pitfall.correct_approach: Verify from_columns exist in the from dataset and to_columns match the to dataset's primary/unique keys

category.name: before_starting
category.item: Understand the business domain and target platforms
Identify all source tables and their columns
Determine which columns are time dimensions
List required metrics and their calculations

category.name: during_implementation
category.item: Add ai_context synonyms for every entity

category.name: before_completion
category.item: Run OSI validator on the model file
Verify all relationship references are valid
Check metric expressions reference correct dataset.field paths
